critiques.summary:
Round 2 was executed well: the decisive discriminator was actually chased (T4), the H2 dual-key mechanism was probed (T5), and caller enumeration was extended (T6). The picture is now: the symptom is a single sharp step at 14:02Z bounded to auth-service's own validate path, flat and undecayed for ~2h at ~36%, with traffic unchanged; api-gateway is the only confirmed caller and co-degrades with the identical signature; order-service is clean; redis-cache and gateway changes are excluded; H4/H6/H7 are properly demoted.

However, the #1-vs-#2 ranking (H1 0.40 vs H2 0.40, an exact tie) is still decided by nothing but the deploy preceding the rotation by one minute. Both candidates are real, verified, contemporaneous auth-service changes and both H1's and H2's mechanism hops remain ASSUMED (F18 says precedent cannot separate them; F24/F30 say the key question is unobservable in the retrieved data). Two cleaner items turned up that are stronger than round 1 suggested: (1) there IS a token-metadata channel nobody tried — per-request trace ids are recorded (F25: unique traces per line, 466 lines), so the rejected requests can be joined to any other telemetry keyed by trace id, and 466 rejects is only a tiny sample of a ~36% failure against ~400 req/s over 2h; (2) T6's enumeration of minting callers was cut off by budget exhaustion, leaving H4 formally un-closed on its only decisive axis. A cross-service trace-id join plus the minting-caller sweep are cheap, answerable, and each can move or eliminate a ranked hypothesis. Also flag a calibration bug: a 'steady ~one line per 10-30s' stream at 466 lines over 2h cannot be the literal 36%-of-400-req/s reject rate (~140/s, ~a million rejects); it must be a sampled/aggregated WARN stream, so any cohort claim drawn from it must be labeled sampled. Note further that the rate does not decay over 2h — this weakens H2's old-kid-circulation story but does not confirm H1's parse-strictness story either, since the same flatness is equally consistent with an unconverged-fleet share.

Verdict: needs_evidence (cap 0.45). If round 3 returns the trace join (old-kid-only vs new-kid included) the ranking can be finalized; if it again returns nothing decisive, degrade to inconclusive on the H1/H2 pair with H1 listed first only on deploy-first ordering, not on mechanism.

challenges.issue: Mechanism hop ('breaking jjwt parser change rejects a deterministic ~1/3 of otherwise-valid tokens via clock-skew default / algorithm or kid strictness') remains ASSUMED. F18 says HIST-109 is precedent only and cannot separate H1 from H2. H1's lead over H2 rests solely on dep-5710 (14:00Z) preceding cfg-2705 (14:01Z) by one minute — a timing tiebreak, not a mechanism. Also, a truly deterministic parser class-rejection predicts near-all-or-none for the affected cohort, yet the observed number is a suspicious ~1/3 — the same awkward number H2 and H5 both need. Plausible but not proven; should not lead H2 at 0.50.

The staged-propagation mechanism is structurally unverifiable in the retrieved data (F24/F30): no key-config/JWKS field exists, no 'jwks'/'identity' service exists (F16/F21), and T5 could not observe whether validators accepted k-2025-10 after 14:01Z. T5 did refute the conventional HIST-108 signature (no rollback, no re-publication, no keys publish, no post-onset config write anywhere), which weakens H2's resolution path but does not refute the failure mode. H2 therefore sits at a tie with H1 on a mechanism that is neither confirmed nor excluded — not defensible as a demoted #2, not defensible as #1 without kid evidence.

Calibration error inflating H1: F28 describes the gateway stream as ~one 401 per 10-30s (466 lines over ~2h) while H1/H2 assert a steady ~36% error rate against ~400 req/s (~140 rejects/s). These cannot both be the same quantity; either the gateway WARNs are sampled/aggregated or auth-service error_rate measures something else. Treating both as literal, mutually corroborating evidence double-counts support. The team should state explicitly which number is the rate and which is a sample; a 466/2h stream is a ~0.017% sample of 36% of ~2.9M requests, so cohort claims drawn from it must be labeled as sampled.

H5 (one bad replica handling ~1/3 of traffic) is not eliminable in current data: F12 and the gaps confirm no per-pod/replica dimension exists for auth-service metrics. But H5 predicts a CONSTANT traffic share failing — exactly the observed flat 2h plateau — so it survives the 'no decay' test that H2 struggles with. Its elimination depends on whether the trace-id join (or any per-pod-enriched telemetry) shows rejects spread across all replicas or concentrated. H5 is ranked 0.12 without that test ever being run.

T6's decisive axis (is a token-MINTING caller also emitting 401s?) was cut off by budget exhaustion; only api-gateway, a validate-forwarding caller, was confirmed. F36 shows no minting tier is even enumerated in the service inventory. H4 is rightly ranked 0.04, but its closing evidence is missing rather than found-wanting — it rests on the absence of a recorded caller-side change, and absences from a budget-truncated enumeration are weak.

H3's first hop ('redis degradation surfaces as invalid_token rather than 5xx/timeout') is assumed (automated check flags it) and its own contradicting findings F17/F11 argue against it. Adequately demoted; just keep it below 0.05.

evidence_requests.question: Join the 466 api-gateway 'invalid_token' WARN trace ids (a ~0.017% sample of the expected ~2.9M rejected requests, so treat as a sample) to per-request telemetry that DOES carry token or key attributes from any other reachable source: check whether api-gateway access logs, the trace/span store, or any span attribute for those specific trace ids records kid, iss, exp, or an auth-service validation error reason. Report the kid distribution in the sampled rejects (all-new / all-old / mixed), and separately whether any of those traces terminated at a specific auth-service instance/pod. A non-empty kid distribution flips the H1-vs-H2 ranking; per-pod trace termination settles H5.
evidence_requests.rationale: This is the single decisive discriminator (H1 vs H2) and the only possible test of H5. T4 found kid absent from the gateway WARN text, but nobody attempted the trace-id join to other stores, and unique trace ids exist in every line (F25).

evidence_requests.question: Complete the auth-service caller enumeration and check each for the invalid_token/4xx signature after 14:02Z: pull the dependency-graph edge list for ALL inbound edges to auth-service (not just the single api-gateway edge in F16), then query error_rate and logs for every caller returned, especially any service that MINTS tokens (portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service, payment-service, settlement-service). Report which callers show the signature and which are clean, and confirm whether any minting tier exists between api-gateway and auth-service.
evidence_requests.rationale: T6 was truncated by budget exhaustion, so H4's only decisive test (does the fault sit upstream in a minting caller) is still unrun, and whether api-gateway is auth-service's sole caller is asserted from a single graph edge.

critiques.summary:
Round 3 did the right things but the environment could not yield the decisive evidence, and the tool budget is now exhausted. What is solidly established: the symptom is a single sharp step (not periodic) bounded to 14:00:00-14:02:00Z, flat at ~35-37% for ~2h with request_rate unchanged [F7,F8,F9]; the fault is confined to auth-service's own token-validation path, with api-gateway as the only confirmed caller co-degrading at the identical minute with the identical single signature [F10,F27,F28,F29,F31,F32,F33,F37,F42]; order-service and all other callers are clean [F11,F34,F29]; shared/upstream causes are excluded (redis-cache is the only shared component and is not co-hit; no gateway/redis config changes; no minting tier exists between gateway and auth-service) [F5,F17,F36,F38,F39,F42]; and only two changes exist all day, both auth-service-side one minute apart — dep-5710 (jjwt 0.11→0.12 + rewritten TokenValidator, 14:00:00Z) and cfg-2705 (kid k-2025-10→k-2026-04, 14:01:00Z) — with no rollback or re-publication of either after onset [F1,F2,F13,F14,F19,F20,F23].

The blocking problem is that the H1-vs-H2 pair is a genuine tie on mechanism, not on timing. The single discriminating fact — whether the rejected population contains only old-kid/unconverged tokens (H2) or also the new kid k-2026-04 (H1) — was chased through every reachable channel and is structurally unavailable: gateway WARN lines carry only a trace id, no kid/iss/exp [F25,F26,F43]; the trace-id join returns only the reject line itself [F44]; auth-service's own store is unreachable (503) [F47]; no keys/JWKS publication record exists for any service and the config API exposes no key material or grace-window field [F21,F24]; the trace-store and pod/iss/exp/kid field probes were never executed due to budget exhaustion, so 'attribute absent' cannot be distinguished from 'store unreachable' [F45,F46]. H1's parse-strictness mechanism remains ASSUMED (HIST-109 is precedent only) and H2's dual-key mechanism remains ASSUMED and unobservable [F18,F24,F30]. The no-decay-over-2h fact argues against pure old-kid circulation but does not confirm H1's rule, since it is equally consistent with an unconverged-fleet share. H5 (partial-fleet) can be neither confirmed nor excluded: no per-pod dimension exists on auth-service metrics [F12,F47]. H4's minting-caller axis is closed by topology (no minting tier, no non-gateway caller) rather than by its own decisive test, but it is demoted. So the causal locus is well-proven; the choice between the two contemporaneous auth-service changes is not, and no remaining query can settle it.

challenges.issue: Mechanism hop is ASSUMED, not evidenced: 'a breaking parser change rejects a deterministic ~1/3 of otherwise-valid tokens' rests only on precedent HIST-109. Nothing shows the rejected set includes new-kid tokens; F26/F30/F43/F44 establish that no reachable source records kid/iss/exp, so H1 is not discriminated from H2 by any retrieved data. Its flatness argument is symmetric — H2's failure mode and H5's instance-share also predict a flat plateau.

Also mechanism-ASSUMED: whether k-2025-10 remained accepted in a dual-key/grace window is structurally unobservable (no key-material/JWKS fields, no keys publisher, auth-service logs down) [F21,F24]. Its core story — steady circulation of old-kid tokens — is weakened by the absence of any decay over ~2h [F28] and by no post-onset re-publication [F19], but weakened is not refuted.

Ranking of H1 above H2 is decided by a one-minute deploy-vs-rotation ordering (14:00 vs 14:01), which is a tiebreaker of convenience: the deploy's code cannot be effective at 14:02 unless rollout completed, and both changes sit inside the 14:00-14:02 onset bound [F8], so ordering alone does not establish which is causal.

Not formally eliminable: no per-pod/per-replica dimension exists on auth-service metrics or gateway lines [F12,F47,F43], and the pod-field probe never executed [F46]. A ~33% bad-replica share predicts the same flat plateau, so it survives on non-observability rather than on being contradicted.

Closed only by topology: no minting tier and no non-gateway inbound edge to auth-service [F37,F38,F42], while payment/settlement/market-data/pricing/user-service/bff-web log content was never retrieved (budget exhaustion). Its decisive minting-caller test remains un-run, so it is demoted rather than refuted.

Calibration/data-quality caveat that must survive any writeup: the 466 gateway WARN lines over 2h (~1 per 10-30s) cannot be the literal 36%-of-400req/s reject stream (~140/s). All cohort claims drawn from it are sample-based, and the stable-single-signature observation (F27) is partly an artifact of a sampled/aggregated stream.
